subject: Notice: High tail latency affecting streaming chat for Furnishly (mitigations + timeline)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@furnishly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: High tail latency affecting streaming chat for Furnishly (mitigations + timeline)

Hi Elena —

Quick heads-up from our side: between ~08:40–09:05 PDT this morning we observed elevated 99th-percentile latencies on the streaming/chat endpoints serving Furnishly (your account id: FURN-112). The impact was intermittent but caused a higher frequency of delayed tokens and occasional stalled streams for a subset of requests.

What we’ve done so far:
- Routed traffic to a warmed edge cluster to reduce cold-KV cache misses.
- Throttled batch sizes for your streaming route to prioritize tail latency (temporary config change).
- Opened RWI internal incident RWI-7894 and started a parallel investigation with infra and runtime teams.

Immediate mitigations for your engineering team (recommended, low-risk):
1) Add short client-side reconnect/backoff (250–500ms) to resume streams after a single stalled chunk.
2) Enable the ephemeral prefix cache header we discussed (x-rwi-kv-prefetch:1) if you can — reduces cold-start tokens.
3) For critical flows, lower max_tokens_per_chunk to 32 for the next 24 hours.

Attachments: incident timeline PDF (summary) and raw streaming latency CSV for the window.

We’ll follow up with a timeline and root-cause once the postmortem is done. I’m on the thread if you want to hop on a quick call.

—Hannah

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether the throttling to smaller batches will affect throughput for our peak? We are expecting a marketing surge midday.
- Can you expose the short-lived header you mentioned as a toggle from the Console so we can flip it in the UI without a deploy?

If helpful we can open a Zoom; I’ve looped in ops and eng.

—Elena

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:02:15 -0700
Subject: RE: Notice: High tail latency affecting streaming chat for Furnishly (mitigations + timeline)

Hannah — quick internal notes for the record and for the postmortem:
- Root-cause hypothesis: transient KV cache thrash on the edge shard serving FURN-112 combined with an autoscaler spin-up lag for warmed pools. We saw simultaneous spikes in backend queue depth and a small number of pinned long requests (seq_len >> median).
- Actions taken: hotfix to route FURN-112 to a warmed locality, reduced batch target to 8 tokens for streaming route, and increased aggressive prefetch on the cluster.
- Impact estimate: affected ~0.6% of your live streams during the 25-minute window; median latency unaffected, 99th jumped from ~320ms to ~2.8s.

Next in post-incident work: capture heap dumps for the edge runtime, add a guardrail that rejects single-streams with >1024 tokens to avoid pinning, and improve autoscaler downscale latency. I’ll own the RCA doc (JIRA RWI-7894).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Notice: High tail latency affecting streaming chat for Furnishly (mitigations + timeline)

Hi Elena —

Answers inline:
- Throughput impact: routing to warmed nodes + reducing per-request batch size will slightly reduce peak aggregate throughput per GPU (~5–8%) but improves user-visible latency. For your planned midday surge I recommend temporarily enabling our burst-capacity reserve (no config change required) — I’ve provisioned 2 extra reserved slots for the window 11:30–13:30 PDT.
- Console toggle: we don’t yet surface the ephemeral prefix prefetch header in the Console as a single-click toggle. As a workaround I can push the header on your behalf for the next 48 hours; if you’d prefer a Console control we can prioritize it as a short feature (ETA 3 business days).

If you want to proceed with the temporary header push and the reserved burst slots I’ll schedule both for 11:00 PDT and send you a confirmation.

Attachment: rwi-incident-timeline-20260504.pdf (summary).

—Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@furnishly.com>, ops@furnishly.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Incident follow-up and next steps (RWI-7894) — Furnishly

Elena / Furnishly ops —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the initial RCA. Summary below and immediate next steps we will take together.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-05-04 08:40 PDT: first elevated 99th-ms latencies observed on streaming chat for FURN-112.
- 08:42 PDT: automated alert triggered; routing fallback engaged for affected requests.
- 08:46 PDT: manual reroute to warmed edge cluster; temporary batch-size reduction applied.
- 09:05 PDT: metrics returned to baseline for majority of requests; small residuals cleaned up by autoscaler.

Root cause (short): a combination of (a) KV cache thrash on an edge shard after an unusual mix of long-sequence requests which pinned runtime resources, and (b) autoscaler cooldown behavior that delayed adding warmed capacity for that locality. The pinned requests increased queueing for the streaming worker which manifested as high 99th-percentile token latency and intermittent chunk stalls.

Permanent mitigations we will implement (ETA / owner):
- Add a per-request length guardrail to reject or split >1024-token streaming requests (ETA: 2 weeks, owner: Runtime team / JIRA RWI-7901).
- Improve autoscaler warm-up and predictive prefetch for spike patterns (ETA: 4 weeks, owner: Infra team / JIRA RWI-7904).
- Surface the ephemeral prefix prefetch toggle in the Console (ETA: 3 business days, owner: Console team / JIRA RWI-7910).
- Dashboard: new streaming-99pct alert and a dedicated heatmap for edge-queue depth (ETA: 1 week).

Mitigations already applied for Furnishly:
- Temporary header push: x-rwi-kv-prefetch enabled for FURN-112 (window 2026-05-06 11:00–2026-05-08 11:00 PDT).
- Reserve burst capacity assigned for your midday window on 2026-05-05 and 2026-05-06 (2 slots).

Impact note and credit: we estimate the event affected ~0.6% of streams; user-visible errors were rare but degraded UX in a narrow time window. As a gesture, I’ve applied a 10% service credit for the affected request hours to your account (visible on your May invoice).

Next steps for Furnishly ops:
- Confirm whether you want the Console-first toggle prioritized (quick feature) or prefer a manual header push when needed.
- Review the attached incident timeline PDF and let us know any questions.

If you’d like, I can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to review the postmortem with your engineering leadership.

Thanks — we’ll keep you updated as the RCA JIRAs progress.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
